reviews.one_line_contribution: It takes the published within-episode 'contextual drag' effect, moves it across the episode boundary into an agent's retrieved memory, and asks whether the harm is carried by the prior trajectory's action content rather than its success/failure label, and whether LLM abstraction (raw -> summary -> insight) strips the failure harm faster than it strips the success benefit, yielding a rule that the right storage abstraction depends on a store's failure fraction.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two verified threats, plus one from the ICL literature. (1) arXiv:2605.29463, 'Honest Lying: Understanding Memory Confabulation in Reflexive Agents' (2026-05-31, verified on both s2 and hf channels) — reflexive agents store confident but incorrect task interpretations and then repeat those errors *despite environment resets*, quantified by a 'Reflection Repetition Rate'. That is essentially P1's copy rate, cross-episode, already measured at the insight/reflection abstraction level; the proposal never cites it. It does not do label dissociation or the abstraction ladder, so it does not fully collide, but it substantially de-risks and thereby de-novels the headline 'drag crosses the episode boundary'. (2) arXiv:2602.04288 'Contextual Drag' (verified, s2, 4 citations) owns the mechanism itself — failed attempts in context bias generation toward structurally similar errors; the proposal's contribution reduces to a setting extension for which no one has offered a reason the boundary would block transmission. (3) For P2 specifically, arXiv:2202.12837 (Min et al., 'Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations', verified via s2cli) established years ago that ground-truth labels in in-context demonstrations contribute little relative to input distribution and format; arXiv:2605.26350 ('When Correct Demonstrations Hurt', 2026-05) updates the same point. 'Content, not label' is therefore the strongly favoured prior, not a surprising claim, and a TOST equivalence result confirming it adds little. On the abstraction side, arXiv:2605.12978 (verified), arXiv:2605.24117 SkillEvolBench (verified) and arXiv:2603.02473 ('Diagnosing Retrieval vs. Utilization Bottlenecks', found via s2cli, not separately verified) all already report that raw episodic storage matches or beats consolidated/summarized storage, which is the direction the proposal's P4/P5 policy rule has to fight.
reviews.strongest_objection: The only genuinely new claim — P4/P5, that abstraction filters failure drag faster than success benefit, so the store's abstraction level should track its failure fraction — is confounded with injection volume, and confounded specifically by a finding this program has already made. Raw trajectory, ~100-token summary and one-line insight differ by roughly an order of magnitude in injected tokens, and the plan only 'reports abstraction token counts' rather than matching them; the sole token-load control is a length-matched *irrelevant* episode, which controls the raw arm against emptiness but never equalises tokens *across* the abstraction ladder. So 'summary removes the failure harm' is fully consistent with 'fewer injected tokens remove the harm', which the brief states as an established result of this very program (cutting injection from seven items to three eliminated the harm from the same bank; volume, not content, was the causal lever). If the abstraction effect is a dose effect, P4, P5 and the failure-fraction policy all collapse into a re-description of the dose-response curve that Q2 already owns. A second, independent hole: P4 defines asymmetry as 'failure harm inside the noise band while success benefit remains above the MDE'. That is the difference-in-significance fallacy — two effects on opposite sides of a threshold are not a demonstrated difference. The claim needs the interaction term (outcome x abstraction) with a CI on the harm-to-benefit ratio as the primary test, and the plan names the mixed-effects model but does not designate that contrast as primary.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Add token-matched abstraction arms: a raw trajectory truncated to the summary's token budget and a summary padded (or a multi-summary bundle) to the raw budget, so the abstraction contrast is run at fixed injected tokens; without this the paper cannot separate its novel claim from the dose-response effect. (2) Re-specify P4 as an interaction/ratio with a confidence interval rather than as one arm inside a noise band and one outside. (3) Add a redaction control — the same failure prior with only the erroneous step removed or replaced by a neutral step — which is the clean isolation of 'error content' and is much stronger than the different-task-type irrelevant episode. (4) Engage arXiv:2605.29463 head-on and state what the copy rate measures that the Reflection Repetition Rate does not; engage arXiv:2202.12837 and explain why P2 is not already the default expectation, or drop P2 to a sanity check and stop billing it as a central claim. (5) Cut scope to fit the node: the design as written is roughly 22 conditions x 500 tasks x 2 seeds x 3 backbones plus a k=3 arm, a stale arm and a 300-task prospective test — on the order of 80k ALFWorld rollouts including a 120B MoE — which does not fit the brief's own 'a few thousand evaluation episodes per configuration' budget on one 4xA100 node. Run the full factorial on 8B, and carry only the decisive cells (raw/summary x success/failure, true label) to 27B and 120B.
reviews.missing_baseline: A token-matched abstraction control — raw trajectory truncated to the summary's token count (and/or summary padded to the raw count). The plan's only load control is a length-matched irrelevant episode from another task type, which does not equalise tokens across the raw/summary/insight arms, so the abstraction-asymmetry result is not separable from an injection-volume effect. A close second, also absent: a control for query-independent action-prior imprinting — a prior whose actions are plausible for the task type but whose specific error is redacted — since the copy indicator as defined (new episode's first error category equals the prior's) can be produced by a generic action prior rather than by transmission of that error; this program's own appendix idea action_prior_imprinting names exactly this confound and the proposal does not address it.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision on the full conjunction (cross-episode drag + label dissociation + abstraction asymmetry), but the check has two specific blind spots I found, and it is not as clean as it presents itself. Queries I ran, all answered by channel (a), the s2cli command (s2 and hf both returned; WebSearch was unavailable in this session and WebFetch is blocked, so channel (b) answered nothing): [1] 'cross-episode contextual drag failed prior episodes agent memory bias new episode errors' -> 2607.10608, 2607.01480, 2608.00017 (Memory Reward Inflation), 2602.04288, 2512.11485, 2605.18421 (EvoMemBench) — no collision. [2] --recent 'failed trajectory in memory transmits error to next task label vs content abstraction summary insight' -> arXiv:2605.29463 (Honest Lying), 2607.13884 (Experience Memory Graph, reuses failed trajectories for correction), 2603.02473 (raw chunks match or beat summarization), 2607.17621, 2607.12747. [3] 'Honest Lying memory confabulation reflexive agents ALFWorld persistent errors across environment resets' -> 2605.29463 confirmed on both channels, plus 2605.20616 (Auto-Dreamer), 2605.12978. [4] 'rethinking role of demonstrations ground truth labels in-context learning' -> arXiv:2202.12837 (Min et al.) and arXiv:2605.26350 ('When Correct Demonstrations Hurt', 2026-05-25). [5] --recent 'abstraction level raw trajectory versus summary versus insight memory injection failure fraction store policy agent' -> nothing on point; nearest were 2608.04574 (spatial memory staleness in VLM agents) and 2607.10608 — genuinely empty for the failure-fraction-conditioned abstraction rule, which is the proposal's best-protected claim. [6] --recent 'contextual drag extended to agent episodic memory retrieved failed episode repeats same error ALFWorld' -> 2605.29463, 2511.12997 (WebCoach, cross-session memory explicitly motivated by agents' repetitive errors), 2505.00234, 2602.04288 — no collision. IDs I verified with s2cli paper: 2602.04288 (2026-02-04, 4 cit), 2607.10608 (2026-07-12, and its Enter-Propagation-Recovery framing is confirmed, which matters because the proposal borrows that trace), 2605.12978 (2026-05-13, 10 cit), 2605.24117 (2026-05-22), 2606.05684 (2026-06-04), 2512.11485 (2025-12-12, ACL). 2605.29463 and 2202.12837 were verified as returned by the s2 channel. IDs the proposal relies on that I did NOT verify individually: 2607.17621, 2606.22844, 2605.24941, 2607.08716, 2607.03441, 2607.01480, 2605.27762, 2608.24794, 2608.10232, 2607.13988, 2607.12747, 2512.02445, 2505.19436 — of these, 2607.17621, 2607.08716, 2607.01480 and 2607.12747 did surface in my own searches with matching titles, so they exist; the rest are unchecked. Judging the check itself: it is more detailed than most (named queries, named IDs, channel labels), and its conclusion happens to survive my searches. But (i) it concedes that its two WebSearch queries 'were issued but not executed' because the budget was exhausted, so the recency channel was single-source; (ii) its content claims about 2602.04288 (11 models, 8 tasks, 10-20% drops, REVISE/FILTER partial) came from a WebFetch of the HF page, which the coordinator forbids — I could verify only the ID and the abstract-level claim, not those numbers, so they should be treated as unverified in the write-up; (iii) it misses arXiv:2605.29463, the single closest cross-episode error-persistence result, in a search set that was explicitly aimed at cross-episode failure transmission; and (iv) it treats the empty label-vs-content search as support for novelty while never touching the in-context-learning label literature (2202.12837), where the answer to P2 is already the strong prior. An empty agent-memory search plus an unexamined ICL literature is not a novelty argument for P2.
